text.p: These are the leading stories in the Albanian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
KOHA JONE
- President Sali Berisha's Democratic Party is leading rebel committees in south, the paper says.
- Editorial calls on parliament to lift the state of emergency, saying Albania is facing a political crisis not a civil war.
- Justice Minister Spartak Ngjela accused the Democrats of breaking the agreement reached by ten parties when they rejected the new electoral law based on a proportional vote.
- A Council of Europe two-page report on Albania says many European politicians have criticised President Berisha and his administration for the crisis.
- Kristaq Luniku, former central bank governor said he had warned Berisha two years ago about the risks the pyramid schemes represented to the country's economic stability.
RILINDJA DEMOKRATIKE
- The Democratic Party is resolved to respect a cross-party agreement reached on March 9 to hold elections in June.
- A resolution of the Council of Europe wants rebel committees to be disbanded as a condition for holding new elections.
- Berisha's government should not be held responsible for tragedy in Albania, an American political analyst says.
GAZETA SHQIPTARE
- An editorial asks whether the economic collapse could also be blamed on the International Monetary Fund whose representative in Albania ignored the activity of the pyramid schemes.
- A small ship packed with 517 Albanians escaping violence and lawlessness Albania reached the Italian port of Barletta.
- Schools will re-open on Tuesday under the protection of armed police, a sign Albania is returning to normal after two months of chaos.
ALBANIA
- Parliamentary elections will be held at the end of June as agreed on March 9, Berisha is quoted as saying.
- Editorial asks Prime Minister Bashkim Fino to distance himself from his Socialist Party which the paper alleges continues to back the so-called rebel committees in the south.
- Rebel-held town of Vlore is turned into hell at night with several gangs terrorising residents, paper says.
- Mother Teresa calls for peace and calm in Albania.
ZERI I POPULLIT
- Albania will not be stable as long as President Berisha remains in power, the German Frankfurter Rundshchau newspaper is quoted as saying.
- Vlore people rallied to commemorate people drowned a month ago when an Albanian ship collided with an Italian navy frigate 30 miles off Brindisi in southern Italy and sank.
